description.p: Zorin Explorer is a native Explorer-style file manager for Linux, designed for Zorin OS and GNOME.

Archives now open in the window like folders, 7-Zip included. A local archive is listed in-process with libarchive, opened directly so it can seek, and its folders are browsed with the same tabs, breadcrumbs and Up as anywhere else. GVfs cannot read 7-Zip because it hands libarchive a stream it cannot seek, which is why a .7z used to leave the window.

Files and folders can be copied or moved out of an open archive into a folder, with the same conflict handling and progress as any other transfer. An archive is read-only, so a move copies the entry out and leaves the archive unchanged.

Extraction and compression now run inside the app. A local archive is handed straight to libarchive, the same library GVfs uses underneath but opened directly so it can seek, which is why 7-Zip and RAR archives extract exactly like ZIP ones and why no archiver program is needed to unpack a .7z. Compression writes ZIP, 7-Zip and tar.gz with pure-Rust writers.
The Debian package no longer recommends zip or p7zip-full. Only gvfs-backends remains, for the remote archives that still go through GVfs.

Right-click ▸ Compress packs the selected local files and folders into a ZIP, 7-Zip or tar.gz archive beside them, using the system's zip, 7z or tar program. The Debian package now recommends zip and p7zip-full.

Extract places an archive's contents in a folder named after it, unless the archive already contains a single folder, which lands beside the archive as it is. .7z archives are unpacked with the 7z program, since GVfs cannot read them.
Everything running is shown in the status bar as a label and progress bar beside the spinner. Click it to list each running operation with its own progress and Cancel button.
Pressing Escape cancels a file drag in progress, leaving the files where they were.
Hidden files stay hidden in the icon grid when hidden files are switched off, and a quick press on a tile starts a drag instead of the rubberband selection.

Sorting by size, date modified or type now works. The folder listing does not carry those, so the sort had nothing to order by and fell back to the name; they are now fetched for every entry when you sort on one of them.
Start typing in the file list to select the first item whose name matches. Pause for a second to start a new search; Backspace edits it and Escape abandons it.

Open With offers the applications that match the file. A file whose type had not loaded yet was treated as an unknown type, which matched almost nothing; the type is now worked out from the file name. In the Flatpak, Other Application opens the system's application chooser, because the sandbox cannot see installed applications.
A Debian package is now published with each release. It is the primary package, since the app needs the host's applications, GVfs, polkit and terminal.

The Flatpak no longer crashes when the window is maximised or resized. It was built without access to the GPU, so the renderer could not start inside the sandbox and the app crashed on the first resize.

Copy, Move, Rename, Move to Trash and Delete work again from the context menu, toolbar and keyboard shortcuts. Folder listings had stopped reporting which actions each file allows, so every one of those commands was disabled.

A large folder such as /tmp no longer freezes the window. Rows the view had bound were evicting each other from a metadata cache that was too small, and each eviction re-asked for the same files, spinning the main loop at full CPU.
File icons match their file type again in small folders and in the icon grid; they had stayed on the generic icon because resolved types never reached those rows.
A refresh of a folder already on screen updates the list or grid in place instead of rebuilding it, so scroll position, focus and selection survive a busy directory.

Archives open in the window. Activating a zip, tar, 7z or rar browses it like a folder, with the archive itself in the path, instead of handing it to another file manager. Zip-based documents such as .docx and .epub still open in the application that owns them.
Going up from the top of an archive returns to the folder the archive is in.
An online account is listed once, under Online accounts, rather than three times: GIO reports one account as two mounts, and both were given rows of their own.
The sidebar reads as a tree: sections are separated and their titles aligned, each level of children is drawn with a guide line, and every row reserves the same column for its arrow so icons line up.
Online accounts lists accounts again rather than every disk, restoring a filter lost when sidebar enumeration moved behind the directory repository.
Remote locations work inside the Flatpak sandbox again: it had no permission to reach GVfs, so every non-local location failed and Browse Network and Online accounts were empty.
Discovered network servers are listed under Browse Network.
Sidebar clicks work while Preferences or Operations is open instead of doing nothing.
Expanded tree arrows no longer keep a pressed highlight.
Attached devices that are not mounted are now listed, and activating one mounts it.
Hot-plugged devices now appear without restarting: the volume monitor was being finalized immediately, so no device signal ever arrived.
